nodes.title: Shortcast — Project README
nodes.summary: Project overview documenting Shortcast, a macOS 15+ SwiftUI app that converts long videos into ready-to-post shorts for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. Covers architecture (WhisperKit transcription → Director LLM → AVFoundation cutting → vertical reframe → publish via Upload-Post or TikTok official API), installation, build-from-source instructions with XcodeGen, model choices (Gemma 4 12B, Qwen 3.5 9B, Gemma 4 E4B), the full processing pipeline diagram, privacy guarantees, known limitations, and acknowledgements. Licensed Apache 2.0.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with embedded ASCII diagrams, code blocks, and HTML badges.
nodes.name: README.md

nodes.title: TikTok Official Publishing Integration
nodes.summary: Technical design document for Shortcast's TikTok official Content Posting API integration. Documents the current manual-token flow (inbox upload via video.upload scope and direct post via video.publish scope), the app settings stored in AppSettings (client key, secret, access token, publish mode, privacy, duet/stitch/comment toggles, AIGC label), the publish behavior (single-chunk upload, inbox vs direct post initialization payloads), known limitations (no OAuth, no refresh tokens, no scheduling for TikTok official), next integration steps (OAuth callback, token refresh, creator-info query, chunked upload), and the PublishingProvider extension pattern for future providers.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with Swift code snippets showing the PublishingProvider protocol pattern and JSON API payloads.
nodes.name: docs/tiktok-official-publishing.md

nodes.title: YouTube & Instagram Official Publishing — Implementation Ideas
nodes.summary: Detailed implementation plan for adding YouTube Data API v3 and Instagram Graph API official publishing providers. Covers the provider-per-platform architecture pattern (vs unified Upload-Post), YouTube resumable upload protocol with chunked upload strategy, Instagram two-step container creation + publish with resumable upload for the hosting challenge, authentication flows (manual token vs in-app OAuth via ASWebAuthenticationSession), Shorts/Reels detection logic, per-platform settings design (YouTube: client key/secret/access/refresh tokens/channel ID; Instagram: access token/user ID/page ID), a unified settings UI with per-platform provider selection, an implementation roadmap (Phase 1 YouTube week 1-2, Phase 2 Instagram week 3-4, Phase 3 multi-provider mix week 5), and key challenges (Instagram video hosting, OAuth token management, rate limits, scheduling complexity, error handling).
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with Swift sketches, ASCII diagrams, API specifications, and phased implementation roadmap.
nodes.name: docs/youtube-instagram-publishing-ideas.md

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand Shortcast's purpose: turning long videos into ready-to-post shorts for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts using on-device ML.

tour.title: App Entry Point
tour.description: The SwiftUI app entry point creates the WorkspaceModel environment object and launches the main ContentView window.

tour.title: Data Models
tour.description: Core data structures: VideoJob represents a dropped video, ClipCandidate is a viral moment found by the Director, ShortClip wraps a clip with editing state, and PostVariant holds platform-specific captions.

tour.title: ML Inference Services
tour.description: On-device ML pipeline: ModelManager handles model lifecycle, MomentFinderService (the Director) finds viral moments using Qwen 3.5, GemmaService runs multimodal captioning, and PromptBuilder assembles LLM prompts.

tour.title: Media Processing
tour.description: Video processing pipeline: MediaExtractor cuts clips, TranscriptionService extracts text (sidecar or WhisperKit), VerticalReframer converts 16:9 to 9:16 with face tracking, and VideoOverlayRenderer burns text hooks.

tour.title: Publishing System
tour.description: Multi-platform publishing: PublishingProvider protocol defines the interface, TikTokOfficialProvider uses Content Posting API, UploadPostClient handles Upload-Post service, with documentation for YouTube/Instagram integration.

tour.title: SwiftUI Views
tour.description: User interface layer: ContentView routes between states, DropZoneView handles video input, ShortsResultsView shows the grid of generated shorts, and SettingsView configures API credentials and preferences.

tour.title: State Orchestration
tour.description: WorkspaceModel is the central state machine coordinating the two flows: caption-a-short (single video → captions) and make-shorts (long video → transcribe → find moments → cut → caption → publish).
